summary: The ported mechanism does not apply at prefill M, and the correctness bound as written rejects the atomic modes anyway, so the expected outcome is PATH CHOSEN = master on both classes, i.e. a wasted check. Ride it on another Marlin-path check as a prepare-only probe instead.
justification: moe gained only at bs=1, where Marlin's grid has far fewer (m-block x n-tile) tiles than SMs and splits K across CTAs, so the fp32 global reduce with locks serialises; at bs 8-32 there it measured flat, and w13 atomic add was neutral 0.987. Here, at T=753 with _align_parallel at bsm 64, w2 has ~32 local m-blocks x 16-32 n-tiles = 512-1024 tiles on 132 SMs, so at most a stripe-boundary tile per SM is K-split and the reduce is a minor cost; at T=3012 even less. Weakest link 1: realistic gain is a few % of a ~230-250 us w2 call (~5-15 us/shape, <0.5% of the turn_1 load) - below the 0.97x pick threshold on the whole _experts_marlin, and turn_1 rows drift 7-10% so it is unreadable in the judge. Weakest link 2: the self-check bound (rel L2 <= 1e-3 vs master's w2 output) is too tight: moe's chosen atomic mode measured 4.79e-3 vs master (bf16 atomic accumulation), so both atomic candidates fail and master is picked. Weakest link 3: 'atomic_zero' adds a 49 MB (turn_1) / 197 MB (turn_4) memset of cache3, 15-65 us, larger than any plausible gain.
confounders: stack-tonight-five-prefill: _align_parallel (local routes only) reduced the m-block count Marlin sees; that is what decides how much K-splitting happens, and it makes K-split rarer, not more common.
interference: If it runs at all, no companion: the prepare A/B prints PATH CHOSEN per class with both times, which is the only readable evidence at this effect size.
rules_flags: Atomic accumulation is nondeterministic run to run; fine under a tolerance check, but the prepare self-check must compare against an fp32 dequant reference with a calibrated bound (~5e-3 vs master, per the moe measurement), not 1e-3.
open_questions: Does sglang's moe_wna16_marlin_gemm zero C internally when use_atomic_add=True (moe's no-memset 'atomic' mode passed its check, which suggests it does)? If so, that internal memset is a fixed cost at prefill M.
How many of w2's tiles are actually K-split at T=753/3012 (Marlin's par/stripe count)? Printing it would settle the mechanism without a check.
builder_instruction: Do not spend a check on it; if wanted, add the per-class prepare probe (bound 5e-3 vs master and fp32-reference-calibrated, print K-split tile count, both times, PATH CHOSEN) as a rider on the next Marlin-path check, e.g. turn-align-remap-on-side-stream-under-pooler.
